Introduction and meaning
Stalking. BNS restatement of IPC 354D. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 354D. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 78 is the rule on “Stalking”. The section provides that (1) Any man who—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 78 exists so that “Stalking” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
78. (1) Any man who—

(i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman; or

(ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any other form of electronic communication,

commits the offence of stalking:

(i) it was pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime and the man accused of stalking had been entrusted with the responsibility of prevention and detection of crime by the State; or

(ii) it was pursued under any law or to comply with any condition or requirement imposed by any person under any law; or

(iii) in the particular circumstances such conduct was reasonable and justified

(2) Whoever commits the offence of stalking shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. (i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman; or
2. (ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any other form of electronic communication,
3. commits the offence of stalking:
4. (i) it was pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime and the man accused of stalking had been entrusted with the responsibility of prevention and detection of crime by the State; or
5. (ii) it was pursued under any law or to comply with any condition or requirement imposed by any person under any law; or
6. (iii) in the particular circumstances such conduct was reasonable and justified
7. (2) Whoever commits the offence of stalking shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine

Exceptions, limitations and provisos
Provided that such conduct shall not amount to stalking if the man who pursued it proves that—

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 78 (Stalking) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 78 (Stalking), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman; or
   (2) (ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any other form of electronic communication,
   (3) commits the offence of stalking:
   (4) (i) it was pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime and the man accused of stalking had been entrusted with the responsibility of prevention and detection of crime by the State; or
   (5) (ii) it was pursued under any law or to comply with any condition or requirement imposed by any person under any law; or
   (6) (iii) in the particular circumstances such conduct was reasonable and justified
   (7) (2) Whoever commits the offence of stalking shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 78 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 78 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

learningObjectives: Master the physical and cyber forms of stalking under BNS s. 78.
Analyze the physical branch: following and contacting despite clear disinterest.
Analyze the cyber branch: monitoring internet, email, or electronic communication.
Examine statutory defences: crime prevention, legal compliance, or reasonableness.
State the penalties: up to 3 years for first conviction; up to 5 years for subsequent.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 78 provides that any man who: (i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman; or (ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking: Provided that such conduct shall not amount to stalking if the man proves that: (a) it was pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime by a person entrusted with such duty; or (b) it was pursued under any law; or (c) in the particular circumstances such conduct was reasonable and justified. Punishment: First conviction: imprisonment up to three years and fine; Second or subsequent conviction: imprisonment up to five years and fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A woman has a right to be free from persistent, unwanted surveillance and obsessive pursuit. Unsolicited physical tracking or electronic monitoring that breaches her autonomy and creates reasonable fear constitutes the crime of stalking.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 78 (corresponding to IPC s. 354D).
Branch 1 (Physical/Direct): Follows and contacts/attempts contact repeatedly despite clear disinterest.
Branch 2 (Cyber-stalking): Monitors the use by a woman of internet, email, social media, or electronic communication.
Three Statutory Defences: (a) Crime prevention/detection by authorized officer; (b) Under legal authority; (c) Reasonable and justified in particular circumstances.
First conviction: Up to three years imprisonment and fine.
Subsequent conviction: Up to five years imprisonment and fine.
essentialIngredients: The accused followed and contacted/attempted contact repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest, OR
The accused monitored her internet, email, or electronic communications.
The conduct was not covered by the three statutory exceptions.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 78 covers both traditional physical stalking and modern cyber-stalking. Under Branch 1, a single approach or accidental encounter is not stalking; it requires repeated attempts to foster personal interaction after the woman has clearly communicated that she is not interested. Under Branch 2 (cyber-stalking), repeated contact is not even required: secretly monitoring her browsing history, installing spyware on her phone, tracking her GPS location, or hacking her social media accounts to track her activities constitutes stalking per se. The section provides three narrow defences, primarily shielding law enforcement officers tracking suspects in official investigations.
examples: Teaching example (Physical stalking): A man follows a female student to her coaching center every day for three weeks, waiting outside and trying to hand her letters despite her repeatedly telling him to leave her alone. Section 78(i) is violated.
Teaching example (Cyber-stalking): A man installs a covert spyware application on an ex-colleague's laptop to monitor her emails, chat logs, and webcam feeds. Section 78(ii) applies directly.
distinctions: Physical stalking vs Cyber-stalking: Physical stalking requires repeated contact despite clear disinterest; Cyber-stalking is complete upon unauthorized monitoring of electronic communication.
Courtship vs Stalking: Courtship stops when disinterest is indicated; persisting after clear disinterest transforms pursuit into criminal stalking.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an individual who created multiple fake social media profiles to send messages to a woman who had blocked his original account is liable under BNS s. 78.
Rule: Under BNS s. 78, repeatedly attempting contact despite a clear indication of disinterest, or monitoring electronic communication, constitutes stalking.
Application: Blocking an account is a definitive indication of disinterest. Circumventing blocks with fake profiles to persist in contact violates s. 78.
Conclusion: The individual is guilty of stalking under s. 78.

shortAnswer: State BNS s. 78 definition of physical and cyber-stalking.
List the two branches: repeated contact despite disinterest, and electronic monitoring.
List the three defences: crime prevention, legal authority, reasonable circumstances.
State punishments: up to 3 years (first), up to 5 years (subsequent).
